newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Klima says won't balk, CA going to top bidder.
newsitem.headline: Klima says won't balk, CA going to top bidder.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima on Thursday said he would not be swayed by increasingly vitriolic political infighting and would sell number two bank Creditanstalt to the top bidder.
"Investment house J.P. Morgan said that the Bank Austria offer is the highest and strategically the best," Social Democrat Klima told his party's annual convention in this southern Austrian spa town.
"And if I don't sell to the highest bidder I automatically break European Union law -- and every Austrian would also have the right to sue me," he added.
Market leader Bank Austria has offered the highest price, the finance minister said, at 16.7 billion schillings for the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt.

But the conservative People's Party, the junior partner in the year-old coalition, favours selling Creditanstalt -- long regarded as a conservative stronghold -- to an international group headed by Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali.
The two parties convene for an emergency session of coalition leaders on Saturday afternoon at the behest of the conservatives to discuss the imbroglio.
